question: Pipette $20$ or $25\text{ cm}^3$ of solution B into conical flask. Add 2 or 3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator and titrate against solution A from a burette to a colourless end point.
Repeat the above procedure twice more using fresh portions of solution B. (16 marks)
Calculate the average titre. (2 marks)
Write the equation of the reaction. (2 marks)
Calculate the molar concentration of $\text{KOH}$ in solution B; (3 marks)
Calculate the number of moles of $\text{KOH}$ titrated; (3 marks)
Calculate the number of moles of $\text{HX}$ consumed in the titration; (2 marks)
Calculate the molar concentration of $\text{HX}$ in solution A; (3 marks)
Calculate the molar mass of the weak acid; (3 marks)
Calculate the relative molecular mass of $\text{X}$ in the formula $\text{HX}$; (2 marks)
Calculate the $\text{pH}$ of solution A. (4 marks)
Distinguish between the end point and the equivalence point in acid-base volumetric analysis. (4 marks)
Explain why phenolphthalein and not methyl orange is used in the above titration. (3 marks)
Give one major source of error in the experiment (a) above. (1 mark)
Give two common features of all volumetric analyses. (2 marks)
You are provided with sample A1 = Benzoic acid. Record the physical characteristics of the sample.

Solubility test: with small quantities of the sample in separate test tubes, determine the solubility of the sample in:
i. water
ii. dilute hydrochloric acid
iii. dilute sodium hydroxide

Functional group test:
i. using a cleaned spatula, heat a small quantity of the sample in a Bunsen Burner flame.
ii. to a small quantity of the sample dissolved in ethanol, add small amount of $\text{NaHCO}_3$, warm the resulting mixture and note any gas evolution. If gas is evolved, test its reaction with lime water.
iii. to a small quantity of the sample dissolved in ethanol, add $1\text{ ml}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and warm the resulting mixture. Perceive the odour of the mixture by blowing air with your hand across the mouth of the reaction test tube.
iv. dissolve a small amount of the sample in ethanol. Dip a moist red litmus paper into a dilute solution of $\text{NaOH}$ or $\text{NH}_3$, the colour changes to blue. Then dip this blue litmus paper into the sample solution. (15 marks)
You are provided with sample A2 = Copper(II) trioxonitrate(V). Carry out two (2) confirmatory tests for the cation.
Carry out two (2) distinguishing tests for the anion. (15 marks)
